subject: Sprint-zero preflight: MAP tasks for POC env (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Subject: Sprint-zero preflight: MAP tasks for POC env (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Hi Natalie,

Per our MAP (mutual action plan) kickoff, attaching a compact preflight for Sprint Zero so we can lock the environment activation window. High-level asks up front:
- org onboarding (Redwood account + admin invite)
- API key issuance + initial key scoping (staging/test only)
- temporary IP allowlist entries for Redwood egress (two CIDRs below)
- VPC peering request details (we can supply the template)

I'm attaching a one-tab checklist (map-poc-preflight-checklist.xlsx) and a VPC peering request template. Proposed timeline: complete the items below by Wed 05/05 so we can begin seeded tests on Thu 05/06 and a canary run on Fri. If anything here is a blocker, flag it and we'll adjust the MAP.

Quick details:
- API keys: request two keys (staging-read, staging-write) with TTL 90 days.
- IP allowlist: add 34.203.12.0/24 and 52.14.88.0/26 for initial testing (we can narrow after canary).
- VPC peering: provide VPC id, region, and desired subnet route table. We will coordinate the acceptance window.

Next step: can you confirm owners for org invite & VPC peering? I suggest Natalie + Chris Li on your side.

Thanks,
Sean

Subject: Re: Sprint-zero preflight: MAP tasks for POC env (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Thanks Sean — received and looks sensible. Quick clarifications from our infra team:
1) IP allowlist: we prefer to add /24s only for monitoring reasons. Can you provide an alternate /24 for the second block?
2) API keys: we need guidance on scopes (read vs generate) — can you share the exact scope names we should request?
3) VPC peering: we can provision the peering request but need the canonical ASN and the route propagation guidance for our cloud router.

Owners: I'll take org invite and API key intake, Chris will own the peering request. Can you send the minimal scopes and the ASN? Also, our security lead will want to review the checklist; can you point to the single-sheet checklist in Drive rather than attaching?

-Natalie

Hi Natalie, Chris —

Great, thanks for the quick read. Answers below and I’ve replaced the attachment with a Drive link per request. See the Drive folder for the living checklist and the peering-template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-map-poc-preflight

1) Alternate IP /24: use 3.120.44.0/24 instead of the /26 previously suggested — that will satisfy your monitoring policy.
2) API key scopes: please request the following labels from the console team: 
   - redwood.api.staging.read
   - redwood.api.staging.generate
   (We recommend stg.read for health checks + embeddings-only workloads; stg.generate for token-generating calls.)
3) ASN & routing: Redwood's canonical ASN for peering is 64512, and we prefer route propagation via static routes on your cloud router. Include the attached vpc-peering-request-template.txt and fill VPC ID, region (us-west-2), and the explicit subnet route table IDs. We'll accept the peering during the 05/05 acceptance window between 10:00-12:00 PT.

Timeline recap (MAP milestones):
- 05/01: preflight checklist shared (today)
- 05/03: BridgeHealth completes org invite + API key request (Natalie)
- 05/05: VPC peering request created (Chris) and accepted during 10:00-12:00 PT slot
- 05/06: Redwood seeded tests (smoke + KV caching)
- 05/07: Canary inference run + joint validation

If that aligns, I'll add these dates to the HubSpot record and create a short validation runbook for post-peering tests.

Sean

Natalie/Chris —

A couple of practical notes from ops to avoid rework during the canary:
- Firewall rule names: please include "rdw-poc-<env>-<date>" so our automation can detect and verify the entries.
- Short TTL on keys: we can accept 90 days but request that the first pair be rotate-on-first-use = true so we capture usage metadata.
- If your cloud router requires a specific MTU for the peering interface, let me know; we typically prefer 1500 but can support jumbo if needed.

I'll be on the 05/05 acceptance window to confirm route table propagation and to run the first traceroutes. If you want, we can do a quick pre-acceptance run on 05/04 to validate DNS and security group openings.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into a green canary.

Ben
